searchText: hi <@397389662085185547> I will continue my question here. So 12.5% is the fixed maximum % change the gas fee can go, and at 100% block fullness, just means 100% of 12.5%? And 0% is the reverse Indeed! That 12.5% comes from the BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR constant (which is 8) Ah I see. Ok thanks I think I understand it better now 🙂 > And 0% in the reverse To be clear, if a block is empty, the base fee goes down 12.5%. It will stay the same if the block is exactly half full in terms of gas used So it’s a linear function from -12.5% to +12.5% from 0 to GAS_LIMIT gas I thought the 12.5% is related to gas fees and GAS_LIMIT is related to the block fullness, two separate things no? Or you meant GAS_LIMIT as in 100% block fullness? so if every block is at GAS_LIMIT, then the gas increases every time by 12.5%. If so then I get you 👍 Yes, the latter. Today, that would be 30M, but if the gas limit went up or down to, say, 40 or 20, then the base fee would be stable at 20M gas used (for a 40M limit) or 10m gas used (for a 20M limit).

And 0% is the reverse

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: That 12.5% comes from the BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR constant (which is 8)

excerpts.author: docker01
excerpts.content: Ah I see. Ok thanks I think I understand it better now 🙂

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content:
> And 0% in the reverse

To be clear, if a block is empty, the base fee goes down 12.5%. It will stay the same if the block is exactly half full in terms of gas used

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: So it’s a linear function from -12.5% to +12.5% from 0 to GAS_LIMIT gas
